findings.expected: Define how loggerd handles the manager's shutdown signal so it remains available to consume each encoder's final watermark, finalize writers and sentinels, and then exits within the existing five-second window. If this cannot work under the existing manager order, state that manager-driven D-16 teardown is infeasible and request a separately reviewed manager-scope decision before claiming it.
findings.observed: IF-10 starts STOP_DRAIN from an isolated test harness while loggerd and encoderd are alive, then stops encoderd before loggerd. AC-16 requires a manager-order proof, but the interface never specifies how loggerd responds when the real manager signals it before waiting for encoderd. The current source order sends nonblocking stop signals to all stopping processes (loggerd before encoderd), then performs encoder-first blocking waits; loggerd's current event loop exits on do_exit and has no drain-on-SIGINT path. A sequential harness drain does not establish manager-driven teardown.
findings.remediation: Architect: revise IF-10 (and its process-lifecycle context) with an explicit manager-SIGINT drain transition, including encoder completion, loggerd's continued consumption, writer/sentinel completion, timeout behavior, and the no-manager-change boundary. If no such path is feasible, mark manager-driven teardown as a hard stop and route any required manager-order change for separate review.
findings.statement: The manager-driven STOP_DRAIN transition is not specified for the actual stop-signal order, leaving whole-process teardown dependent on behavior the build owner would have to invent.
findings.verification: Review the revised IF-10 against the current Manager.ensure_running stop sequence. Confirm AC-16 exercises the actual concurrent signal order, verifies loggerd remains alive through final acknowledgements and output finalization, and applies the five-second limit; otherwise confirm the package explicitly stops and requires separate manager-scope approval. Rerun the design shape and boundary validators.

findings.expected: Separate prerequisites that can be proven before source changes from integration behavior that exists only after S1. Either provide a concrete pre-implementation probe that exercises the same manager-signal drain behavior without implementing the product change, or place the manager-driven end-to-end drain proof in S1/AC-16 and make it a hard stop before S2 or any performance work.
findings.observed: AC-13 makes proof of managed STOP_DRAIN within five seconds a condition before implementation. S1 and the implementation spec then introduce the drain protocol and require the first manager shutdown proof. The package does not identify a pre-implementation probe for that new loggerd/encoderd behavior; the described isolated capability probe is not defined to exercise the manager's signal sequence.
findings.remediation: Planner: revise the S0/S1 dependency and AC-13/AC-16 checks so pre-code MPP, VisionIPC, queue, and static manager-order feasibility work is distinguished from testing the newly implemented signal-driven drain. Preserve a hard no-go if S1 cannot pass under the existing manager order; do not proceed to the corrected-copy reference or performance stages after a failure.
findings.statement: AC-13 requires proving manager-driven STOP_DRAIN before implementation, while the only specified STOP_DRAIN path is introduced by the later S1 implementation, so S0 has no defined target for this proof.
findings.verification: Confirm the acceptance table names the exact pre-implementation evidence and the exact S1 concurrent-shutdown test, with manager predicates/order unchanged and a five-second pass condition. Confirm S2 depends on that S1 pass. Rerun the design shape and boundary validators.

findings.expected: Specify an independent first-pass oracle for the S1 correctness repair, including expected per-ID segment assignment and the D-13 event, audio, and decoded-media checks, or otherwise make the stage ordering establish a valid reference before any criterion depends on it. The first S1 run must not validate itself or rely on the known-lossy run as a qualifying baseline.
findings.observed: AC-15 requires comparing segment assignment and D-13 outputs during S1. The plan disqualifies the saved 144-submitted/138-emitted run under D-16 and says not to compare against the lossy baseline; AC-17 only establishes repeatable corrected-copy output ledgers in S2 after S1 passes. Neither AC-15 nor the implementation spec defines the independent expected output/segment oracle for the initial S1 pass.
findings.remediation: Planner: define how the initial corrected-copy repair proves every required D-13 output field and per-ID segment mapping without a prior qualifying run; align AC-15, IF-7, and the implementation spec to that oracle. Keep AC-17 as the later repeatability/reference stage and retain the hard D-16 gate before candidate comparison.
findings.statement: AC-15's S1 D-13 output and segment checks lack a usable reference: the lossy 144/138 run is disqualified, and the corrected-copy reference is established only in later S2.
findings.verification: Check that the revised S1 test can derive its expected ID, segment, log, audio, and decoded-media results before launching the first corrected-copy run, and that S2 alone establishes the repeatable reference used by candidate comparisons. Rerun the design shape and boundary validators.

escalation.reason: D-17 is satisfied by a complete explicit no-go: the exact-target evidence cannot be obtained and no runtime scope satisfies retained D-13/D-16 correctness and D-15 paired KA2 proof. The canonical design-to-build workflow permits APPROVED only when a build can consume the design, while r6 explicitly has no implementation slices; there is no repairable package defect to send back as REVISE. Keep the build boundary closed and route this package for no-go phase/run closure. Reopen design only after the stated exact-target evidence becomes available or the user explicitly changes the objective or proof requirements.

R6 is a coherent explicit no-go but cannot cross DESIGN-to-BUILD: it has no build slices, and the phase verdict is ESCALATE. Keep build closed and route the no-go for closure; any future implementation requires new exact-target evidence or a new explicit user decision changing the objective or proof requirements, followed by a new approved design revision.

basis.ref: conditional frontend/UI handoff applies only when a user-facing surface exists

findings.statement: The shape check reports the frontend/UI handoff as UNCHECKED. This is a backend recording-path change with no user-facing surface, and the manifest carries the architect's sanctioned typed no-surface applicability record.

The canonical shape-check path resolves through skillset-saves to /data/media, outside /data/openpilot, so the validator refuses that path before reading it. A fresh in-project mirror of the current r8 package artifacts passed the shape check with zero failures and the two expected conditional findings; the boundary validator independently checked the canonical manifest and all artifact hashes. The mirror only worked around the path containment rule and did not replace the submitted artifacts.

The real KA2 V4L2 exporter, DMA-BUF fence behavior, and live camera buffer reuse remain unqualified. The package correctly limits its proof to isolated synthetic DMA-BUF tests and records live-camera qualification as deferred under D-29; build evidence must not claim those live-source guarantees.
